findings.title: Memory type can overstate or understate durability
attack_path: A volatile claim is stored under a slow-decaying memory type.
The type profile retains a higher recency score.
The claim can rank above appropriately typed evidence.
evidence: Prompt 115 accepts only the existing closed MemoryType and no payload-authored durability override.
Confidence, source reliability, validity, conflicts, and relevance remain independent score components.
findings.recommendation: Require governed source-freshness evidence and benchmarked record-level overrides in Prompt 116.

findings.title: Missing source freshness is reported rather than inferred
attack_path: A record has a recent local timestamp but an old external source.
A naive assessor labels the source fresh.
evidence: Every Prompt 115 assessment emits source_freshness_state unavailable.
The policy anchors on effective validity and never labels a source verified.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the unavailable state until observation and source evidence are first-class.

findings.title: Decay assessment has no mutation or execution authority
attack_path: An operator assesses an old memory.
No archive, delete, supersede, refresh, tool, shell, or network operation is available from that result.
evidence: KnowledgeDecayPolicy is stateless and the CLI is read-only.
findings.recommendation: Treat future automated refresh as a separately authorized workflow.

findings.title: Old globally scored cache entries are invalidated
attack_path: A cache contains a result scored under the old global half-life.
A version mismatch prevents the old result from being served as current.
evidence: Existing cache validation binds algorithm identity.
findings.recommendation: Continue bumping the identity for scoring-contract changes.

limitations: This review does not prove that the default day values optimize retrieval accuracy.
Source freshness and observation provenance are not yet stored.
Memory type correctness remains dependent on governed write paths.
